Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

All bags are sticks.

All trees are papers.

Some sticks are papers.

**Conclusions:**

II. Some papers are trees.

III. No bags are papers

options.text: Only conclusions I and III follow

questions.question: Mawsynram in the ______ of the Khasi Hills receives the highest average rainfall in the world.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Southern**__** part.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mawsynram:**

 
 
• Mawsynram is a town located 69 kilometers from Shillong, the state capital of Meghalaya state in northeastern India, in the Southern Khasi Hills area.
 
• In India, Mawsynram experiences the most rainfall.
 
• It is said to be the wettest site on Earth, receiving** 11,872 millimeters of rain **on average per year.
 
• The **Guinness Book of World Records states that Mawsynram saw 26,000 millimeters of rain in 1985.**
 
• Mawsynram is a popular tourist destination known for its scenic beauty, waterfalls, and limestone caves.
 
• Traveling to Phlangwanbroi village enables nature enthusiasts to go deep into the jungle, which is home to colonies of protected Hoolock Gibbons.
 
• Worldwide, **Krem Puri is the world's longest sandstone cave.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khasi Tribe:**

 
 
• **An ethnic group in northeastern India's Meghalaya state is known as the Khasi people.**
 
• **Khasi Hills** are home to the Khasi people
 
• They are one of the few South Asian populations **speaking Austronasiatic**.
 
• One of the few tribes in the world that still practice matriarchy is the Khasi tribe.
 
• Khasi region is also known for its tea and orange plantations.
 
 
 
• **There are three possible causes for Mawsynram's heavy rainfall:**
 
 
• During the monsoon, warm, humid winds from the Bay of Bengal push northward, covering a large area before being forced to converge into a tighter zone over the Khasi Hills, where they concentrate their moisture.
 
• The Khasi Hills' east-west alignment puts them squarely in the line of the Bay of Bengal breeze, which causes a considerable uplift as well as cooling, additional condensation, and consequently more rain.
 
• Lastly, during the monsoon season, uplift over the Khasi Hills is almost continual due to strong winds in the upper atmosphere continuously drawing the lifted air upward, which results in nearly constant rainfall.

questions.question: The Legislative Council of a state assembly __________ of the total number of members in the legislative of the state and in no case fewer than 40 members.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**one-third.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India's legislature is divided into two houses.
 
• **Article 169 of the Constitution allows the states to have a Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) in addition to the Legislative Assembly ( Vidhan Sabha), much as Parliament has two Houses (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha).**
 
• Article 169 (Abolition or creation of Legislative Councils in States): Parliament may by law provide for the abolition of the Legislative Council of a State having such a Council or for the creation of such a Council in a State having no such Council, if the Legislative Assembly of the State passes a resolution to that effect by a majority of the total membership of the Assembly and by a majority of not less than 2/3rd of the members of the Assembly present and voting.
 
• **A state's Legislative Council may not have fewer than 40 members or more than one-third of the State Assembly's total membership, as stated in Article 171 of the Constitution.**
 
• At present, 6 States have a Legislative Council: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, and Karnataka.
 
• The tenure of a Member of the Legislative Council (MLC) is 6 years, with 1/3rd of the members retiring every two years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Manner of Election of Members of the Legislative Council (MLC)**: **Article 171**

 
• **The state's MLAs elect 1/3rd of the MLCs.**

questions.question:
Which of the following forms an asset for a bank?

I. Reserves

II. Loans
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An asset is something of value that can be owned by an individual or an organization and can be used to produce something profitable.
 
• For a bank, these are the resources that generate income and profit.
 
• A bank has assets such as cash held in its vaults and moneys that the bank holds at the Federal Reserve bank (called “reserves”), loans that are made to customers.
 
• Other assets for a bank can include investments, such as stocks and bonds, and physical assets, such as buildings and equipment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Reserves, which are the funds held by the bank to meet its obligations and cover any potential losses, are considered an asset for the bank.
 
 
• **This is because the reserves can be used to make loans or investments that generate income for the bank.**
 
• These are important for a bank because they act as a buffer against unexpected losses.
 
 
• **Banks are required by regulatory authorities (like the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in India) to hold a certain amount of reserves to ensure financial stability. e.g., CRR (Cash Reserve Ratio) and SLR (Statutory Liquidity Ratio).**
 
 
 
 
 
• Loans are also considered an asset for the bank.
 
 
• When a bank makes a loan, it expects to receive interest payments from the borrower over time. This interest income is a source of revenue for the bank and is considered an asset.
 
 
 
• **Reserves are typically low-risk and low-return, while loans are higher-risk and higher-return.**

questions.question: Which among the following folk dances is popularly known as the 'stick dance'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kolannalu.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kolannalu:**

 
 
• **India is home to a number of popular folk dances, including the well-known Kolannalu stick dance from Andhra Pradesh. **
 
• The narrative of the wicked spirit Basavasura that transformed into deity assisting others is explained by the song, dance moves, and background music.
 
• The Kolannalu traditional dance is sometimes referred to as kolkolannalu and is widely known among the Andhra Pradeshi people as Kolattam in Telugu.
 
• It is also known as the "stick dance" because the performers use long sticks (called kolatams) as props during the dance.
 
• Kolattam is a traditional dance in which eight to forty ladies take part. The dancers follow the direction of a leader who forms two circles.
 
• **The dance is performed by the inner circle dancers striking on stickers while the outside circle dances around the sticks.**
 
• **Other Folk Dance of Andhra Pradesh:**
 
 
• Bhagotam
 
• Burrakatha
 
• Kuchipudi
 
• Bhamakalapam
 
• Butta Bommalu
 
• Dappu
 
• Perini
 
• Tappeta Gullu
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ghodemodni:**

 
 
• **An essential type of warrior folk dance, ghodemodni is performed in Bicholim (Goa) during Shigmo.**
 
• It is a reflection of the rich fighting heritage that the Maratha community, who came from the Ghat region, inherited. 
 
• Every member of the Ravalnathkar, Madwal, Saterkar, and Mahamayakar groups participates in this folk dance during Ghodemodni, dressing as a horse and donning white garments. 
 
• It is performed by men and women, and involves intricate footwork and rhythmic movements.
 
 
 
• **Theyyam:**
 
 
• Theyyam is one of the several dance styles that Kerla is famous for.
 
• **The word for God in Malayalam, daivam, is the source of theyyam.**
 
• Despite being a dance style, it is not performed for amusement.
 
• This is a ceremonial performance of centuries-old worship—a dance of the gods.
 
• This dancing worship, which is primarily practiced in Kerala's northern regions, aims to bring divine and mankind together.
 
• Prior to calling upon the deity, the (mostly) male dancer gets dolled up in cosmetics and clothing.
 
• Then he looks into his own reflection in a tiny mirror he's holding in his palm. We refer to this action as mukha darshan.
 
 
 
• **Koli:**
 
 
• **One of Maharashtra's most well-known dance styles, Koli gets its name from the Kolis, the state's fishermen.**
 
• Fishing and the sea, two activities that this community is most familiar with, are incorporated into the dance.
 
• Men and women separate into groups of two and perform this dance style.
 
• These fisherman use this dancing form to depict the motion of rowing a boat. In addition, the dancers simulate the motion of the waves and the launching of nets to capture fish.
 
• The women who work as fishers are positioned in the opposing rows, reaching out towards men with linked arms.

questions.question: Trade agreement between two parties is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**bilateral**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A bilateral trade agreement is a pact between two parties, countries, or regions that outlines the terms and conditions for trade between them.**

 
 
• In it, both parties agree to reduce or eliminate trade barriers such as tariffs and quotas to promote trade and investment.
 
• It can help to increase economic growth, create job opportunities, and improve the standard of living in both countries.
 
• **India-UK Free Trade Agreement (FTA) and the India-UAE Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) are examples of bilateral agreements.**
 
 
 
• Trade Agreements** **are treaties in which a country promises to engage in fewer trade protections with another country (or countries) to engage in more trade.
 
 
• It can be between two countries or between many countries.
 
• Important terms of trade between them include tariffs, quotas, restrictions on imports and exports, and provisions such as trade facilitation, intellectual property rights, and investment protection.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A multilateral trade agreement involves three or more countries or regions that agree to reduce or eliminate trade barriers.
 
 
• **The Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP), among the 15 members, is an example.**
 
• **The World Trade Organization (WTO) is another example of a multilateral trade agreement.**
 
 
 
• A tripartite trade agreement involves three parties, usually countries or regions, that agree to promote trade and investment between them.
 
 
• The North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) is an example of a tripartite trade agreement between the United States, Canada, and Mexico.
 
 
 
• **A unilateral trade agreement is a decision made by one country or region to reduce or eliminate trade barriers without the agreement of another party.**
 
 
• This is usually a preferential arrangement that a developed country makes for imports from developing countries.
 
• The United States has unilateral trade policies under the Generalized System of Preferences.

• **LED Lamps:**

 
 
• It stands for** ****Light Emitting Diode** Lamps. 
 
• **Compared to incandescent light bulbs, LED lighting products provide light up to 90% more effectively. **
 
• Visible light is produced when an electrical current flows through a microchip, illuminating the small light sources known as LEDs. 
 
• Heat sinks are used by LEDs to absorb their own heat and release it into the surrounding air. This prevents LEDs from burning out or overheating.
 
• Compared to both incandescent and fluorescent lights, the lifespan of commercial LED lamps is far longer.
 
• **Unlike incandescent and CFL light sources, which release light and heat in all directions, LED light sources are "directional," meaning they focus their light emission in a single direction.**
 
• This implies that LEDs can use light and energy more effectively in a variety of applications.
 
• All LED products that have been awarded the ENERGY STAR have undergone testing to guarantee that, regardless of the heat sink design, they effectively manage heat to maintain light output until the end of their rated life.

• Heat and ultraviolet (UV) light are produced by this process.
 
• When the UV light hits the phosphor coating inside the lightbulb, it is converted to visible light.

• A metal filament within an incandescent lightbulb is heated by electricity to a "white" temperature, a process known as incandesce.
 
• Consequently, 90% of the energy in incandescent bulbs is released as heat.
 
• They are not typically promoted as an energy-saving option.

questions.question: The Consumer Protection Act provides for a ___________ tier Consumer Disputes Redressal Agencies in India.
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Consumer Protection Act, 1986**:

 
 
• The historic Consumer Protection Act, passed by the Indian Parliament in 1986, is a significant piece of socio-economic law that aims to promote public welfare by allowing consumers to engage directly in the market.
 
• The Act's goal when it was passed was to give greater protection to consumer interests. Its purpose was to protect customers from unfair business practices and other forms of abuse by offering them effective and efficient safeguards.
 
• It **encompasses all industries viz. public, commercial, and cooperative—and all goods and services**.
 
• **The following rights were enshrined in the Act:**
 
 
• Right to Safety
 
• Right to be informed
 
• Right to Choose
 
• Right to be Heard
 
• Right to seek Redressal
 
• Right to Consumer Education
 
 
 
• **Three-tiered Consumer Disputes Redressal agencies are established in India under the Consumer Protection Act. They are as follows:**
 
 
• **District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum** (value of goods or services involved is up to Rs. 20 lakhs)
 
• **State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission **(value of goods or services involved is between Rs. 20 lakhs and Rs. 1 crore)
 
• **National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission** (value of goods or services involved is over Rs. 1 crore)
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• On August 6, 2019, the Parliament passed the historic Consumer Protection Bill, 2019 with the goal of addressing the new issues that customers face in the digital age and offering prompt and efficient administration and resolution of consumer complaints.
 
• The President of India has signed the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
 
• **Salient feature of Consumer Protection Act, 2019**:
 
 
• Inclusion of e-commerce, since e-commerce transactions were not expressly covered by the previous Act.
 
• Section 2(7) defines "consumer" more broadly, encompassing both offline and online transactions.
 
• The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) will be established under the New Act in order to regulate matters pertaining to consumer rights violations, unfair trade practices, and deceptive or false advertisements that harm the interests of the public and consumers. Additionally, the CCPA will be responsible for promoting, safeguarding, and enforcing the rights of consumers as a class.
 
• Filing of complaints electronically online.
 
• The New Act streamlines and expedites the dispute adjudication process by offering mediation as an Alternate Dispute Resolution tool.
 
• **Enhanced three-tiered Consumer Disputes Redressal agencies are established in India under the Consumer Protection Act. They are as follows:**
 
 
• District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum (value of goods or services involved is up to Rs. 1 crore)
 
• State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (value of goods or services involved is between Rs. 1 crore and Rs. 10 crore)
 
• National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (value of goods or services involved is over Rs. 10 crore)

questions.question: Agriculture and fishing activities belong to which sector?
questions.solution:

__
 
• Products and services are produced as a result of economic activity, and sectors are collections of economic activities categorised according to certain standards.
 
• Based on ownership, labour conditions, and the type of activity, the Indian economy can be divided into several sectors.
 
• **Economic sector types according to the type of activity:**
 
 
• **Primary Sector**
 
• **Secondary Sector**
 
• **Tertiary Sector**
 
• **Quaternary Sector**
 
 
 
• **Primary Sector**:
 
 
• Activities in the primary sector of the economy involve the direct use of natural resources.
 
• Some examples of this industry are agriculture, mining, fishing, forestry, dairy, and so on.
 
• It is thus named because it serves as the foundation for all other goods.
 
• It is also known as the "agriculture and allied sector" because the majority of the natural products we use come from forestry, fishery, dairy, and agriculture.
 
• Because primary activities require working outside, those who engage in them are referred to as red-collar workers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Secondary Sector:**

 
 
• It encompasses the sectors in which natural resources generated in the primary sector are used to create final goods.
 
• This sector includes operations such as sugar cane production, cotton fabric production, and industrial production.
 
• Therefore, manufacturing is the sector of a nation's economy that produces goods as opposed to raw materials.
 
• This sector is also known as the industrial sector because it is connected to several industries.
 
• Blue collar workers are those who perform auxiliary tasks. 
 
 
 
• **Tertiary Sector:**
 
 
• The primary and secondary sectors benefit from the activity of this sector.
 
• Economic activity in the tertiary sector assists or supports production rather than producing commodities on its own.
 
• It is also known as Service Sector.
 
• The industry includes things like banking, insurance, finance, and truck or train-borne freight.
 
• It adds value to a product in the same way as the secondary sector.
 
• White collar jobs are those in this industry.
 
 
 
• **Economic sector types depending on labour conditions:**
 
 
• **Organised Sector**
 
• **Unorganised Sector**
 
 
 
• **Organised Sector:**
 
 
• Employees in this industry are guaranteed employment and social security, and job terms are regular and set.
 
• It may also be described as an industry that is registered with the government and to which certain acts are applicable to the businesses.
 
• The organized sector includes hospitals and schools.
 
• Employees in the organized industry are guaranteed a job. They have a set amount of hours that they are required to work. The company must give them extra pay if they put in more hours.

questions.question: A, B and C can finish a work in 10, 15 and 30 days, respectively. In how many days can A finish the work if he is assisted by B and C both every third day?

C can finish a work in 30 days

**Concept:**

Total work is calculated by the LCM of the time taken by each, and total work done in a day is the sum of each's work done in a day.

**Solution:**

⇒ Total work = LCM of 10, 15, 30 = 30 units

⇒ Work done by A in a day = 30/10 = 3 units

⇒ Work done by B in a day = 30/15 = 2 units

⇒ Work done by C in a day = 30/30 = 1 unit

⇒ Total work done in 3 days = 3 + 3 + (3 + 2 + 1) = 12 units

⇒ Total work done in 6 days = 12 + 12 = 24 units

So Remaining work = 30 - 24 = 6 units

On 7th and 8th day, A works and complete the work = 3 + 3 = 6 units

Work completed in 8 days = 24 + 6 = 30 units = Total work

**Hence, A can finish the work in 8 days when assisted by B and C every third day.**

questions.question: The numerator of a fraction is decreased by 25% and the denominator is increased by 25%. New fraction is how much percentage less than the original fraction?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the original fraction be 100/100 = 1.

New Numerator = 100 − 25 = 75

New Denominator = 100 + 25 = 125

New Fraction = 75 ÷ 125 = 3/5 = 0.6 (which is 60% of the original).

Percentage decrease = (1 − 0.6) × 100% = 40%.

**∴ The correct answer is 40%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numerator of a fraction is decreased by 25%.

The denominator of the fraction is increased by 25%.

**Formula Used:**

Percentage Decrease = [(Original Value − New Value) ÷ Original Value] × 100%

**Calculations:**

 
 Original Fraction = 100%
 
 
 New Fraction = 60%
 
 
 Decrease = 40%
 
 
 
 

 
 
 

 

 
 Decrease = 100% − 60% = 40%

⇒ Let the original fraction be x / y.

⇒ New Numerator = x − (25/100) × x = 0.75x

⇒ New Denominator = y + (25/100) × y = 1.25y

⇒ New Fraction = 0.75x ÷ 1.25y = (75 ÷ 125) × (x / y) = 3/5 × (x / y)

⇒ Decrease in fraction = (x / y) − [3/5 × (x / y)] = 2/5 × (x / y)

⇒ Percentage decrease = [{2/5 × (x / y)} ÷ (x / y)] × 100%

⇒ Percentage decrease = 2/5 × 100% = 40%

**∴ The correct answer is 40%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change

Percentage change is calculated as [(Final Value − Initial Value) ÷ Initial Value] × 100. A negative result indicates a decrease, while a positive result indicates an increase.

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is sequentially changed by x% and then by y%, the net percentage change can also be found using the effective formula: Net Change = x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100.

Fraction to Percentage Conversion

To convert a fraction into a percentage, multiply it by 100. For example, the fraction 3/5 expressed as a percentage is 3/5 × 100% = 60%. Therefore, any value that drops to 60% of its original has observed a 40% reduction.
